name: 1729 Prairie Avenue — the George M. Pullman house (K01; refined by T-1881)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B stone (blue) dwelling (D), large and irregular'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

built.note: The marker: 'George M. Pullman Residence. Built 1870-1876'.

research_note: The George M. Pullman house at the north-east corner of Prairie Avenue and 18th Street, moved off the district draft onto K01 by T-1880 under the draft's own id: the 1911 sheet's main block in brownstone, two storeys over a raised basement under a slated mansard with cresting, its north-west and 18th Street pavilions, the Prairie portico and the south-east block, read through the solved camera of the Detroit Publishing photograph (LC-D4-12551, between 1890 and 1901). The sheet's ranges and stable east of the house stay at the draft's massing as pullman_house_1729_prairie_ranges until T-1934; the conservatory is its own K13 record. docs/RESEARCH/k01-1729-pullman-1880/README.md.

documented_range.note: The 1904 target to the 1911 sheet that draws the house: the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), and the Detroit Publishing photograph (between 1890 and 1901; after 1893 by the monument it shows) shows the same main block. Its building and loss dates are not read here.

position.symbolic_location: 1729 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1729 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).
position.note: The rear north corner of the K01 main body: the draft's origin moved 2.43 m north along its own v axis, to the conservatory's south wall (lot frame u 43.750, v -5.930 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, whose own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.611 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line; v runs SOUTH, from the north wall toward 18th Street.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main block read off the 1911 sheet's trace (s20fp-1729-b1 p3) in the house's frame: its west (Prairie) front at u 27.8, its north wall at v 0, where the trace runs at v -2.3 to -3.3 (in the draft's frame) behind the conservatory's south wall (pullman_house_1729_prairie_conservatory, at the draft's v -2.43, which the block stops against), its south (18th Street) wall at v 17.7-18.1 and its east wall at u 0. The north-west pavilion, the 18th Street pavilion and the portico stand on it as K08 projections and the door's porch; the one-storey block at the south-east corner is a K01 rear wing; the ranges and stable east of it are pullman_house_1729_prairie_ranges.

stories.note: Two full storeys over a raised basement under a mansard, as the photograph shows on both street faces; the sheet's '3B' counts the mansard storey (as it does at 1801 and 1816).

construction.note: '3B stone (blue) dwelling' on the 1911 sheet; the photograph shows dressed ashlar on the Prairie front and the 18th Street flank alike.

stone_front.note: Brownstone, the register's material for 1729 (frontage register row pa-1729-5, K02's sandstone_brown), laid in smooth courses as the photograph shows on both street faces, over a two-course base to the basement lights' heads. The rusticated quoins of the photograph's pavilions are not laid (open in the match record).

principal_floor_m.note: Read through the photograph's camera (data/reference_views/pullman_house_1729_prairie/detroit_det_4a08065.json): the portico's balcony floor, at the second floor, stands about 6.6 m over grade and the stoop rises about 2 m from the walk.

storey_heights_m.note: Through the photograph's camera: the balcony floor (the second floor) about 6.6 m over grade and the cornice's top about 12.0 m at the south-west corner (y 300 px against grade at y 500, 16.7 px/m there), over a deep frieze above the second-storey windows' heads (10.5 m).

wall_thickness_front_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: a dressed-stone front's thickness inside the contract's masonry range (0.23-0.45 m), taken at its top for a three-storey stone house; no source gives it.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: as the front's; no source gives it.

service_wall_brick.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the common brick K01 lays where a stone house's service walls are not seen (the rear wing); the photograph does not see the rear.

street_front_trim.note: K09 dresses none of the Prairie front's windows (T-3157): each is named off the Detroit print (street_front_windows), round-arched, the second storey's under their rings. The side walls keep K01's plain stone lintels, the photograph's arched heads on the 18th Street flank being T-3160's.

wall_head.note: The photograph's deep stone cornice, run round both street faces and on round the walls it does not see; its modillions are not laid (open in the match record).

roof_form.note: The photograph's steep slated faces round both street fronts under a deck ringed with cresting: a mansard.

roof_pitch_deg.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the deck behind the cresting, which no picture sees, inside K05's mansard_upper range.

eave_overhang_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the cornice's projection, taken at K01's ordinary value; the photograph shows a deep cornice but its depth is not measured through the camera.

mansard.note: Through the photograph's camera: the lower faces rise from the cornice (about 12.0 m) to the curb under the cresting (about 16.8 m at y 240 px), steep and straight; iron cresting about 0.8 m high round the deck (y 222-235 px). T-3157: four round-arched dormers, read on the dormers' own plane (0.1 m in from the cornice's face): on the Prairie face the centre one's light at x 455-468 px (v 11.0-11.9) between pilasters at x 449-477, its crown at about 14.8 m (y 266) and its sill on the cornice (y 299), built as a 0.9 x 1.7 m arched light in a 0.35 m surround at v 11.45; the south pavilion's narrower one at x 502-518 (v 14.3-15.3), built 0.6 m in a 0.2 m surround at v 14.8; on the 18th Street face two at x 592-604 and 618-630 px, which this oblique view puts at u 21.7-23.8 and 16.5-19.0 to within about 2 m (built at u 22.75 and 17.7). The print draws the Prairie dormers arched and the flank ones too small to read their heads, so the flank's are taken arched like the front's; the Prairie ones' segmental hoods and ears over the arch are not laid (L-k01-1729-pullman-heads-3157). T-3158: the north-west pavilion's own dormer, at x 322-338 px on its section of the mansard (v 0.8-2.0 through the camera), built as the flank's: a 0.8 x 1.6 m arched light in a 0.3 m surround at v 1.5 (0.1 m off the print's centre, the nearest the hip lets a face stand), its crown read at about 15.3 m (y 273), within the reading of the others'.

roof_covering.note: Slate on the lower faces, as the photograph's coursed grey faces read; the deck behind the cresting is not seen and is reconstructed as tin.

stair_tread_m.note: RECONSTRUCTED: inside the contract's stair range; no source gives the treads.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The sheet's portico, 3 m deep in front of the west wall, its floor the landing the columns stand on.

stoop_width_m.note: T-3159: the sheet's stoop (s20fp-1729-b1 p1-p2, 2.6 x 3.4 m), which the Detroit print shows rising between the portico's two northern columns; the portico's floor carries on either side of it as the entrance's terraces (entrance_kit).

entrance_bay.note: The door stands in the Prairie front's north bay (K01's 'south' end is v 0, the north wall, in this house's frame), under the portico, which the sheet draws over v 1.6 to 10.6.

front_bays.note: Through the photograph's camera, along the Prairie front from the north wall: the door's bay between the rusticated piers at x 380 and 413 px (v 5.2-7.8), the centre bay's tall window at x 450-472 (v 10.4-11.9) and the south bay's window at x 520-528 (v 15.5-15.8).

side_bays.note: The north flank's windows, which no picture read here shows.

north_bays.note: The 18th Street flank's windows either side of its porte-cochere and pavilion, counted from the Prairie corner; the photograph sees this face too obliquely to place them. T-3160: round-headed, as the print's flank windows read (their arched heads at y 355-365 px over the arcade's balustrade, x 600-660, under 5 px a metre along the face), each storey's laid once at the sash contract's sill and height; the window at s 6.0 moved to 5.0, clear of the porte-cochere's west end. Their moulded hoods are under a pixel in this picture and are left to the closer views (T-3161).

rear_bays.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the east wall's windows, which no picture read here sees, two across the part beside the south-east block.

sash_by_storey.note: Through the photograph's camera: the centre bay's second-storey window from about 7.8 to 10.5 m over grade (y 378 and 335 px at 16.0 px/m); the principal storey's, behind the ivy, are taken as tall.

chimneys.note: RECONSTRUCTED as a whole, its third stack read off a photograph (T-3161): the 18th Street flank's great stack is read off J. W. Taylor's photograph no. 1445 (the album print a16-aic-taylor-album-pullman-p69 and the print a16-aic-taylor-pullman-from-nw, one negative) through its solved camera (docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/pullman_house_1729_prairie/taylor-1445-camera.md; the prints are link-only in the library, so the camera waits on the rights question on T-3161 before it joins the image gate): a stone stack standing on the flank's cornice and carried up the mansard's face, x 487-522 px at its base on the cornice (y 272-292) against the corner pier at x 447: its west side and south face together 35 px, at 18 px a metre along the flank there and 19 px a metre across it, so a 1.1 m face on the flank's line at u 24.25-25.35 with its 0.8 m west side seen beside it; its moulded cap at y 160, 18.7 m through the camera (the curb at about 16.9 m), a band under the cap. The 1890 Albertype plate shows the same stack rising behind the tree just east of the corner pier. Its depth across the wall line is not measured: 0.8 m, standing on the cornice in front of the mansard's face (its inner face 0.14 m clear of the deck's curb at v 17.46, so the cresting runs behind it) with its outer face 0.47 m out, inside the 0.6 m cornice, as the photograph shows it standing proud of the slope. The deck stack at (20, 13.3) is read from the same three pictures: the Detroit print and the Albertype plate, both from the crossing's south-west corner, show a tall stack rising behind the cresting just WEST of the south-west corner pier (Detroit x 528-545 px, top y 222, against the corner at x 557-560; the plate x about 1293, top y 213, against its corner at 1312), which no stack on the flank's line can do from there; their common line of sight passes the deck at about u 20, v 13.3, where Taylor's camera hides a stack wholly behind the flank stack, as that photograph shows (it shows only cresting either side of it). Its top through the two cameras is 19.05 and 19.9 m, taken at 19.5 (top_m); its place along the line of sight is good to about 1.5 m. It was a reconstructed stack at (18, 12.5) until T-3161. The flank stack is not in the 1890 plate, which is earlier than Taylor's photograph (1890s, after the 1892 additions it shows east of the flank): it is read as later work and stands in 1904. The stack at (10, 5.5) remains RECONSTRUCTED: through all three cameras it stands under the deck's edge, so no picture shows or excludes it. L-pullman-1729-flank-stack-3161.

rainwater.note: RECONSTRUCTED: one copper downpipe on the rear wall; none is read off the photograph.

window_kit.note: RECONSTRUCTED: two-over-two sash, the kit's ordinary pattern; the photograph does not resolve the glazing bars. T-3157: the street front's round-arched lights glazed as K06's round fanlight sash (its wide two-light one at the second storey's centre); the print does not resolve their bars either.

entrance_kit.note: The portico the sheet draws 3 m deep in front of the Prairie front (v 1.6 to 10.6), built as the door's hood on columns: the photograph's columned portico carrying a balustraded balcony at the second floor (y 380-395 px). T-3159, through the Detroit print's solved camera (data/reference_views/pullman_house_1729_prairie/detroit_det_4a08065.json; the portico's front at u 30.6, 13-14 px a metre): the portico is the front's brownstone, not painted joinery (fabric stone), its balcony railed by a stone balustrade (the print's posts and balusters at y 380-390 over the entablature at 390-400, x 343-395; railing_fabric stone, 0.7 m, its rail clear under the second-storey sills). Its columns: the print shows two clear of the ivy and the trees, a lit round shaft at x 374-381 (v 6.9) and one at x 322-330 (v 3.05), both standing on the portico's floor at y 470; the south half is lost in the ivy, so the row is carried on at the print's pitch, a column at the hood's south end (v 10.03) and one between (v 8.5), four in all (the count is the match record's 'four or more'; the two south positions are a bounded design, L-pullman-1729-portico-3159). The flight: the sheet's stoop (s20fp-1729-b1 p1-p2) is 2.6 x 3.4 m, and the print's steps (x 300-370, y 465-490) rise between the two read columns, its north cheek's raked top running from x 335 y 465 down to x 298 y 488 (v about 3.7): a 2.6 m flight centred at v 5.0 (stoop_v_m), and the rest of the portico's floor terraces at the landing's height either side of it out to the hood's ends.

boundary.note: The photograph's low stone wall along the Prairie Avenue line, on piers at the walk. T-3160: and on round the corner along 18th Street on the lot's south line (side_return), the print's low stone wall at x 640-685 px, 0.9 m as the Prairie run, from the corner back to x 35.0 (the print's x 693, u 35.0), where the print's run of posts on a lower curb begins (not built: its posts and rail are too fine to read here). T-3205: the walk's way through it. Through the print's camera (data/reference_views/pullman_house_1729_prairie/detroit_det_4a08065.json) the wall stops either side of a gap at x 195-225 px between two square piers standing over its top (x 180-195 and 225-237), on the street line at s 4.9-6.5 and 3.9-4.9, 6.5-7.6: square before the stair (its axis s 5.0), which the print shows behind the wall at x 300-370. Built as an opening s 4.9-6.5 between 0.6 m piers 1.2 m high (the print's piers stand about 0.6 m over the 0.9 m wall, 1.5 m; 1.2 m is the kit's ceiling for a coping run, within the 0.3 m bar). RECONSTRUCTED: the piers' section (liberty L-k14-walks-1700-block-3205).

bays.note: The sheet's north-west block (u 22.8-27.8, flush with the Prairie front, out to v -1.53: built 1.2 m out, a pavilion's most, 0.33 m short) and the 18th Street pavilion (u 9.5-19.75, 2 m out on the sheet; built 6.0 m wide and 1.2 m out, a pavilion's most, centred on the sheet's, the rest open in the match record), both carried full height under the main cornice as the photograph shows them; the round bay on the north flank (u 15.8-19.7) is not built. T-3160: the 18th Street pavilion moved 1.375 m east (centred at s 14.5, 11.5-17.5) so it stands clear of the porte-cochere (porte_cochere, s 6.35-11.48), still inside the sheet's u 9.5-19.75; its lights round-headed as the print's flank windows are (K06's round fanlight sash).

rear_wings.note: The sheet's one-storey 'B' block at the south-east corner (u -2.0 to 0, v 11.6-18.8), laid in brick behind the stone house.

street_front_windows.note: T-3157: the Prairie front's street windows read off the Detroit print through its camera (data/reference_views/pullman_house_1729_prairie/detroit_det_4a08065.json; the front's plane u 27.75, v along it from the north wall, 14-16 px a metre), each on 5-6x crops. Second storey: three round-arched lights between the rusticated piers, the north one over the portico at x 390-402 px (v 6.0-6.9), the centre one the widest at x 452-472 (v 10.6-12.0) and the south one narrow at x 519-528 (v 15.2-15.7); their sills at about 7.5-7.8 m (y 380-382) and their crowns at about 10.1-10.3 m (y 339), each arch under a moulded ring (x 447-473 at the centre, about 0.25 m out from the light), laid as K02 voussoirs flush but for 0.05 m, with a keystone barely larger, since the print's 15 px a metre does not part a moulding from a ring of stones (L-k01-1729-pullman-heads-3157). Principal storey, behind the ivy: the centre light's arched head at y 411 (5.8 m) over a sill hidden at about y 468, and the south one's at y 418 (5.3 m); the ivy hides their surrounds, so their arches carry none, and the centre one is held 1.2 m wide so its head stands clear of the portico's south end (v 10.6). The north bay's principal storey is the door under the portico. Widths are the lights between the jambs' dark edges plus a sash frame each side.

basement_lights.note: RECONSTRUCTED: the raised basement's lights are not laid on the Prairie front (T-3157): the Detroit print shows none, the street wall and the ivy standing in front of the basement, and the front's windows are named one by one off the print (street_front_windows), which takes no area lights.

street_front_pavilions.note: T-3158, through the Detroit print's solved camera (data/reference_views/pullman_house_1729_prairie/detroit_det_4a08065.json): rusticated piers divide the Prairie front into pavilions at x 363-380, 412-428 and 497-515 px, which put them at v 3.96-5.26, 7.65-8.82 and 13.67-14.89 on the front's plane; the third is built to 14.74, 0.15 m short of the reading, where the south windows' voussoir rings stand. The south-west corner is turned by the same banded stone (x 545-560, v 16.9-17.9), built as a corner pier returned 1.1 m onto the 18th Street flank. The piers rise from the base's coping to the cornice's bed, banded in channelled courses that step in and out (the print's long-and-short banding; its rhythm here is reconstructed at 0.5 m courses, 0.05 m channels, a 0.1 m step and 0.12 m proud, below what the print's 16 px a metre resolves), and break the deep frieze between the second storey's heads (about 10.6 m) and the cornice (about 12.0 m): its bed course at 10.72-10.84 m and a framed panel in it between each pair of piers (the panels' number and framing reconstructed: the print reads the frieze as a band of shadowed panels). A row of modillions under the cornice's corona (x 435-520 px, y 309-313, read as a dotted band), laid all round the cornice at a reconstructed 0.5 m pitch, 0.12 m wide and 0.22 m out. Raised ribs on the mansard's Prairie face over the first two piers (x 369-379 and 413-423 px), so the roof reads in sections over the bays; their 0.45 m section and stone colour reconstructed. The curb's step between the sections (2-3 px, about 0.15 m) is under the good-enough bar and not built (L-pullman-1729-pavilions-3158).

porte_cochere.note: T-3160, through the Detroit print's solved camera (data/reference_views/pullman_house_1729_prairie/detroit_det_4a08065.json): the arcade on the 18th Street flank (x 598-685 px) is a one-storey block standing out from the flank, not arches in its wall. Its west end is seen nearly square to the camera (its round arch is as wide as it is high, about 15 px a metre either way), its south front edge-on past the corner pier (about 5 px a metre along it). Its west face meets the flank at x 598 (u 21.4, s 6.35); the west arch's jambs at x 610 and 645 put it 0.81-3.18 m out (span 2.37 m), its crown at y 410 and springing at about 428 (6.0 and 4.85 m); the corner pier at x 645-668 and the south front's arch at x 668-678 put the front 4.27 m out and its arch at s 7.78-10.05 (span 2.27 m); the pier at x 678-685 ends where the tree and the building beyond take over (s 11.7). The entablature's soffit at y 402 (6.5 m), the balustrade's base at y 397 and its top at 389 (about 6.85 and 7.4 m). The block's east end is a bounded design: closed at s 11.48 by a corner pier the size of the west one, with an arch mirroring the west end's, so the carriage passes through (L-pullman-1729-porte-cochere-3160). The 1911 sheet draws the one-storey 'porte-cochere' (s20fp-1729-b1 p4) at u 15-20, 2-5.4 m out (s 7.75-12.75), 1.4 m east of and 1.1 m further out than the print's; the print, the nearer witness to what stood, governs the build, and the disagreement is written into the match record.

yard.note: T-3205 (the owner, 2026-10-27: walks, gates and boundaries to the pictures). The walk in flags from the stair's foot out to the wall's opening, where it jogs 0.7 m south behind the wall to pass between the piers (the opening reads 0.7 m south of the stair's axis), and on to the public walk; the lawn across the front. RECONSTRUCTED: the walk's flags, their width and wear, the lawn and its bare strip are the K14 kit's (data/components/prairie_1904/k14_condition.json) aged from the phase's own year, as the kit's rule is; liberty L-k14-walks-1700-block-3205.
